core_obligations: Reduce to the two conditions characterising a sheafification: an element of O(X) mapping to zero in F(X) is killed by an h covering, and an element of F(X) is locally in the image of an element of O (proof lines 12094-12100).

Settle the first condition: f maps to zero in F(X) exactly when f|_{X^{awn}} = 0, which means f is locally nilpotent, so the closed subscheme cut out by f gives a surjective closed immersion of finite presentation, i.e. an h covering (proof lines 12101-12104).

Settle the second: after passing to an affine open X = Spec(A) an element of F(X) lies in A^{awn}, and the universal homeomorphism limit lemma produces a ring map A -> B of finite presentation with Spec(B) -> Spec(A) a universal homeomorphism such that the element is the image of b in B, so the singleton family is an h covering; the ph case follows in the same manner (proof lines 12105-12116).
proof_roadmap: Record that the rule is already a ph sheaf with a canonical map from O (proof lines 12089-12093).
Reduce to the two local conditions for a sheafification (proof lines 12094-12100).
Prove the two conditions, one from local nilpotence and one from a finitely presented universal homeomorphism (proof lines 12101-12116).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme S and a big h site as in the definition, the lemma identifies the rule X -> Gamma(X^{awn}, O_{X^{awn}}) as the sheafification of the structure sheaf, and asserts the same for the ph topology (statement lines 12076-12086). The proof already knows from the preceding ph-sheaf lemma that this rule is a ph sheaf, hence a fortiori an h sheaf, and that there is a canonical map O -> F of presheaves of rings (proof lines 12089-12093). It then reduces the sheafification statement to the two standard conditions: that an element mapping to zero is killed by an h covering, and that an element of F(X) is locally in the image of an element of O (proof lines 12094-12100). The first is dispatched by noting that f vanishing on X^{awn} means f is locally nilpotent, so the closed subscheme cut out by f is a surjective closed immersion of finite presentation, which is exactly an h covering; the second by passing to affine X = Spec(A), using that an element of F(X) lies in the absolutely weakly normal quotient A^{awn}, and spreading it out to a finitely presented universal homeomorphism A -> B by the universal-homeomorphism limit lemma, whose singleton family is an h covering (proof lines 12101-12115). Converting the sheafification statement into the two local-surgery conditions and sourcing each from a different input is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
